prompt: Let $P,Q,R$ be classical propositions; $\top$ means true, $\bot$ means false, and $\equiv$ means equal truth values under every assignment. What is the exact dual of $P\lor(Q\land\top)\equiv P\lor Q$? Exchange $\land/\lor$ and $\top/\bot$ throughout, preserving variable positions, negations, and parentheses.

answers.explanation: Duality exchanges both connectives and both constants throughout the identity. Here the inner conjunction becomes disjunction, true becomes false, and both outer disjunctions become conjunctions.
The connectives were exchanged, but true was not exchanged with false. This proposed identity even fails when the first input is true and the second false.
The constant was exchanged, but the connectives were not. This proposed identity fails when the first input is false and the second true.
The inner conjunction also needs to become disjunction. As written, the left side is always false, while the right side need not be.
This consistently renames the two variables. Renaming preserves validity, but it is not the specified duality operation.
This reverses the two sides of the original identity. It does not exchange any connectives or constants.
This substitutes the negation of each variable into the original law. The dual instead keeps variables unchanged and exchanges connectives and constants.
Negating both sides preserves an equivalence, but it is a different transformation from the specified structural dual.
This can result after simplifying the dual, but it is not the displayed formula obtained by the specified exchanges while preserving parentheses.
This is equivalent to the dual after additional commutative rewrites. The specified duality operation preserves variable positions and does not perform those rewrites.
